audience: The team's sprint review: developers and the product owner, who know Whaleshark but not this sprint's work.
notes: Whaleshark is a development environment that runs Pi coding agents on machines you own. You use it from a desktop or web client.
This sprint's work: Settings is a single window opened from the gear in the sidebar footer, with every page listed in one navigation rail.

The rail lists Overview, Connections, Hub, Appearance, Notifications, Providers, Agents, Skills, MCP servers, Text and prompts, Worktrees, Quick commands, Projects, Telemetry, Feature flags and Archive.
Appearance shows the color scheme (System, Light, Dark) and the themes.
Skills and MCP servers are kept per machine and shared across the machines you connect.
The demo runs on a web client acting as a hub with no machines connected, so the Skills and MCP servers pages show loading placeholders, not a list. Do not describe their contents.
Next sprint: populating Skills and MCP servers from connected machines in the demo, and covering more pages.
